carnage.name: LeftyMurph
carnage.commentary: Pulled the card on 5: a par 3 turned into a gross 5 with no shot trail to hide behind. That’s the kind of one-hole faceplant that sticks out when the rest of the round was mostly just ordinary pain.

carnage.name: Bravos99
carnage.commentary: The sixth was the damage spot: par 3, gross 4, no shot sequence logged, just a clean little bogey-shaped bruise on the card.

carnage.name: Golfnut7413
carnage.commentary: He found the weirdest flavor of mess on 7, where a par 3 became a gross 4 and net 5. When the scorecard says bogey plus a net bogey, that’s a double-helping of not getting away with it.

carnage.name: Wardus
carnage.commentary: Hole 2 was the early leak: par 3, gross 4, no shot data, just an immediate bogey slapped onto the opening stretch.

carnage.name: titogreenbrough
carnage.commentary: The third hole was the bad one, a par 3 that somehow turned into gross 4 and net 5. Not a blowup, just the kind of single-hole bleed that keeps adding up like a cheap tab.

carnage.name: Rhino
carnage.commentary: Openers are supposed to settle you in, and instead hole 1 handed over a par 3 bogey with a gross 4 and no shot log to argue with. That’s how you start by stepping on the rake.

players.name: titogreenbrough
players.tagline: Found the greens, then kept three-putting the vibe into the lake.
players.body: This was a net-plus gross-minus kind of round for titogreenbrough, and net is the only thing that matters in this league. He landed at +8 net, with the gross card at +4, and the underlying stuff says the ballstriking actually showed up: +2.01 approach, +2.60 short game, and a solid +4.60 tee to green. The problem was the putter and the ugly counting stats that came with it: 28 putts, 2 three-putts, and six bogeys. He did get 8 greens in regulation and hit 79 feet of putts made, but the card still had the stink of missed chances, especially the par 3 on 3 that became a net bogey and the handful of other over-par holes that kept him pinned in the mud. This is his first completed profile-eligible event, so there’s no trend to sell you yet, just a round where the tee-to-green numbers were better than the finish.

players.name: Bravos99
players.tagline: The putter did the heavy lifting while the rest of the bag mostly stood there blinking.
players.body: Bravos99 took the net at +8, while the gross card was a much prettier +1, which tells you the raw golf was way cleaner than the league result. The stat line backs that up: +4.02 putting, +1.17 approach, +1.74 short game, and +6.93 total, with 25 putts and zero three-putts. He also only had 2 bogeys against 1 birdie, so the card wasn’t a full collapse; it was more like too many pars getting stubborn instead of turning into birdies. The problem is the net finish still drifted to the wrong side because the round never produced enough damage-free scoring to cash in on that good putting. Hole 6 was the worst hole, a par 3 bogey, and he also got dinged again on 17. In the tiny sample from last week, this is a sharp bounce in the raw stats from a +2.50 total appearance to +6.93, but with only one prior start, that’s a maybe-not-a-pattern rather than gospel.

players.name: LeftyMurph
players.tagline: Hit enough greens to tease you, then still swallowed the scorecard like a champ.
players.body: LeftyMurph posted +8 net with a gross finish at +4, which is about as polite a way as possible to say the ballstriking showed some teeth and the score still came out ugly. He gained everywhere except the tee box, with +2.25 approach, +0.89 short game, +0.78 putting, and +3.14 tee to green, plus 9 greens in regulation and 29 putts. That’s the annoying kind of round where the components are better than the card, because the birdie count never got moving enough to offset four bogeys and one double. The big bruise was hole 5, where a par 3 turned into a gross 5 and net 5, and that was the worst hole on a card that never fully escaped mediocrity. With no prior completed profile event, there’s no trend line to pretend is real yet; this is just a round that had enough tee-to-green competence to be less bad than the leaderboard number suggests, but not enough actual scoring to matter.

players.name: Rhino
players.tagline: Three greens in regulation and a whole lot of “well, shit” after that.
players.body: Rhino finished at +9 net and +9 gross, and that’s not a typo in the vibes: the card was rough enough that the gross and net are basically holding hands in the same ditch. The stat sheet is ugly where it counts: -2.80 approach, only 3 greens in regulation, 9 bogeys, and just 49 feet of putts made, with no birdies to break the spell. The saving grace was a little short-game and putting resistance, with +1.36 around the greens and +0.36 putting, but that’s just trying to mop up after the house already burned down. Hole 1 set the tone with a bogey on a par 3, and the rest of the round never really stopped asking for more medicine. This is his second completed profile-eligible event, and the mixed history is now pretty obvious: the prior start was net +5 and gross +5 with brutal short game, this one had better short game but worse ballstriking and a worse net result. That’s volatile, not clean, which is golf’s favorite way of saying “good luck figuring this dude out.”

players.name: Golfnut7413
players.tagline: Ballstriking was screaming; the scorecard still managed to roll its eyes.
players.body: Golfnut7413 ripped the gross side to +1, but the net result still landed at +9, so the league math ate the good golf and spat out a worse finish. The underlying numbers are loud: +7.26 approach, +5.74 tee to green, 13 greens in regulation, and only 3 bogeys, which is the profile of somebody hitting the ball like a grownup. The catch is the rest of the round was inefficient as hell: 32 putts, no sand saves needed, and only 2 birdies, so all that approach juice didn’t get converted into enough scoring. Hole 7 was the worst hole, a par 3 bogey, and he also bled another pair of bogeys on 12 and 14, which is how a good ball-striking day still gets mugged by the card. In his second completed profile-eligible event, the trend is very clear: the approach work jumped from solid to stupid-good, but the net finish got worse because the scoring package didn’t keep up. That’s not a slump; that’s a guy being punished for not cashing checks his irons wrote.

players.name: Wardus
players.tagline: The putter showed up, the irons mostly filed an absence form.
players.body: Wardus finished +9 net with a +4 gross, and that split tells the whole story: enough scoring scraps to look competent, not enough ballstriking to survive. He actually gained +2.88 on approach and +2.88 putting, but the rest of the round got dragged down by -1.83 short game, just 6 greens in regulation, and 6 bogeys. The 104 feet of putts made jumps off the page, so there was some real make-noise in there, but it couldn’t offset the fact that he was constantly trying to clean up messes instead of creating birdie chances. Hole 2 was the first leak, a par 3 bogey, and he kept stacking them on 6 and 7 before at least grabbing a couple of birdies late. With one prior completed appearance, the profile is still small, but the movement is interesting: last week he was basically elite in the short game and putting with a +8.5 total, and this week that edge shrank while the ballstriking got shakier. That’s not a clean upward or downward line, just a reminder that the bad stuff comes back fast when the irons stop cooperating.
